page: Amazon Web Services m8i.12xlarge is a general-purpose server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 48 vCPUs, consisting of 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The x86_64 architecture is supported by a large L3 cache of 480 MB, a 2 MB L2 cache, and a 48 KB L1d cache. The instance is equipped with 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and network connectivity is delivered via a 22 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark data indicates strong performance across memory and computational tasks. The DDR5 memory subsystem achieves a strong read-only small block cached bandwidth of 3825.86 GB/sec and a large block uncached read bandwidth of 195.84 GB/sec, though large block write bandwidth is average at 79.26 GB/sec. CPU performance is highlighted by strong Geekbench scores, including a single-core score of 2209.0 and a multi-core score of 19971.0. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), contribute to top-tier performance in image processing and text processing.

The instance demonstrates strong capabilities in database operations, with a PassMark database score of 24101.52 and Redis SET operations reaching 89.2 million operations per second. It also shows strong performance in software compilation and static web serving throughput at 79.6 GB/sec. For machine learning, the hardware supports prompt processing and text generation for small and medium LLM models, though text generation for large 70B models drops to an average of 3.15 tokens/sec. Given the lack of local NVMe storage and dedicated GPUs, this instance is best suited for memory-intensive general-purpose workloads, enterprise databases, web serving, and CPU-based inference rather than heavy storage-bound or GPU-accelerated tasks.
description: Amazon Web Services m8i.12xlarge is a general-purpose instance featuring 48 vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. It includes 192.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz, providing a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, but lacks local storage and dedicated GPUs. Network performance is supported by a 22 Gbps baseline bandwidth. Benchmark results show strong performance, particularly in memory bandwidth, software compilation, and database operations, with Redis SET operations reaching 89.2 million operations per second. The processor's Intel AMX and AVX-512 extensions enable top-tier performance in image and text processing, as well as strong prompt processing for small and medium language models. This instance is highly suited for enterprise databases, static web serving, software development pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
